records.title: Eryndor — Planetary Fundamentals
records.summary: A five-continent, magically alive world, approximately 50,000 km in diameter.
records.body:
Eryndor is approximately 50,000 km in diameter and 157,080 km around. Its surface is 60% water and 40% land. A 24-hour day, 360-day year, and four roughly 90-day seasons govern the working calendar.

The older 13,400-km diameter, 42,000-km circumference and 71%-water model are superseded.

Everyday experienced gravity, hydrology, weather, agriculture and biology resemble ordinary physics; the explanation for familiar surface gravity on so large a planet is still undecided. World magic is a deliberate fantasy exception.

records.title: The Five Continents
records.summary: Avarra, Tharvorn, Sahrad, Orundel, Vaelora.
records.body:
Avarra is Gloin Hammerfeld's principal campaign continent. Tharvorn is northern, Sahrad southern, Orundel eastern and Vaelora western. Every continent contains multiple peoples, states and traditions.

Twin Titans dry-land shares: Avarra 32%, Orundel 28%, Tharvorn 12%, Sahrad 12%, Vaelora 11%, islands and separate archipelagos 5%. No island territory should be counted twice. Coastlines, countries, mapping scales and precise intercontinental routes await further survey.

records.title: World Tone and Creative Rules
records.summary: Dark and gritty yet hopeful; no species is uniformly good or evil.
records.body:
Eryndor contains exploitation, conquest, famine, prejudice and catastrophic loss, alongside friendship, celebration, scholarship, rescue and reform. Consequences matter. Fantasy-scale cities and heroes are allowed without requiring Earth-historical ceilings.

Long-lived peoples can have large families; birth rates are not silently adjusted. A person may devote a century to a craft or choose domestic life; cultures have distinct expectations. No single trait determines everyone in a people. The creator can revise accepted canon with explicit supersession and a retained change log.

records.title: Ages Versus Eras
records.summary: Worldwide Ages are not the same as continent-specific historical eras.
records.body:
Five worldwide Ages are recognized; the current one is the Fifth Age. Each civilization may name and subdivide historical time differently. The Second Age's Awakening, Wonder and Fire divisions are Avarran conventions, not mandatory world calendars.

The campaign's date is Autumn Day 22, Year 3847 of the Era of Crowns, within the Fifth Age. That year number must not automatically be counted from the global beginning of the Fifth Age.

records.title: Current World Population
records.summary: 2.0628 billion modeled residents across 28 numerical categories.
records.body:
The current sixfold planning census contains 2,062,800,000 modeled residents: Avarra 1,019,760,000; Tharvorn 171,000,000; Sahrad 282,222,000; Orundel 393,600,000; Vaelora 196,218,000. This replaces a 343.8-million draft.

Global Khazari 144 million, Eldar 108 million, Urakai 186 million, humans 960 million. The Seven Khazari Throne domains total 132 million and are INCLUDED within worldwide Khazari; Karak-Varn's 22.8 million are included within the Thrones. Drakari, Aelwyn and Living Mountains are not precisely enumerated.

This is a worldbuilding resimulation, not sudden births or a confirmed omniscient census. Metro-versus-domain boundaries need reconciliation.

records.title: World Geography Awaiting Remapping
records.summary: A vast planet needs resurveyed roads, coastlines, maps and densities.
records.body:
The adopted 50,000-km world and the Twin Titans land allocation supersede earlier diagrams. Broad historical geography and relative regional relations survive, but many route lengths, schematics, old (x,y) throne coordinates and map-image scale bars are still provisional.

Exact river sources, political boundaries, coastlines, local population envelopes and long-distance voyage durations require later consistent mapping. Illustrative maps do not establish canon by themselves.

records.title: First Age
records.summary: Its length is unknown and no authentic contemporary records survive.
records.body: Its length is unknown and no authentic contemporary records survive. Old stories describe extraordinary prosperity, but their historical accuracy is unverified. It ended when the First Great Cataclysm destroyed or shattered moons. Lost moon-specific magics did not return.

records.title: First Great Cataclysm
records.summary: Catastrophic alteration of the earlier lunar system ended the First Age.
records.body: Catastrophic alteration of the earlier lunar system ended the First Age. Destroyed moons permanently ended their associated magical powers; fragments of some shattered bodies became new moons and new magical sources. The exact collision mechanism and old moon count remain unknown.

records.title: The Second Age — Avarran Chronology
records.summary: Exactly 1,437 years worldwide, divided in Avarran histories into Awakening (1–321), Wonder (322–1,321) and Fire (1,322–1,437).
records.body: Exactly 1,437 years worldwide, divided in Avarran histories into Awakening (1–321), Wonder (322–1,321) and Fire (1,322–1,437). Other continents may use different names, eras and date boundaries.

records.title: Era of Awakening
records.summary: Years 1–321 in Avarran chronology.
records.body: Years 1–321 in Avarran chronology. Peoples rebuilt after lunar disruption, learned to support their societies through mundane agriculture, engineering, records and sanitation alongside surviving magic. Unequal recovery, famine, exploitation and reform all occurred.

records.title: Era of Wonder
records.summary: Years 322–1,321 in Avarran chronology.
records.body: Years 322–1,321 in Avarran chronology. A thousand-year flourishing of new fragment-moon magics, engineering, art, education, medicine, trade and great kingdoms, with continuing inequality, conflict and reform. The destroyed First Age magics were not recovered.

records.title: Era of Fire
records.summary: Years 1,322–1,437 in Avarran chronology.
records.body: Years 1,322–1,437 in Avarran chronology. Exiled dark mages transformed fertile southeastern Avarra into the Southern Wastes and created its volcano. Elsewhere, independent kingdoms and cultures continued their own histories. This era is NOT blank: dedicated annals and regional histories exist.

records.title: Southern Wastes Dark Mages
records.summary: At the start of the Era of Fire, communities exiled mages who had accessed dark magic.
records.body: At the start of the Era of Fire, communities exiled mages who had accessed dark magic. The mages gathered in southeastern Avarra, destroyed fertile farming land by magic, created a volcano and lived in isolation without external diplomacy or trade. The mages survived far into the Third Age. Their identities and ultimate fate remain open.

records.title: End of Second Age — Global Earthquakes
records.summary: In Second Age Year 1,437, planet-wide earthquakes struck Eryndor.
records.body: In Second Age Year 1,437, planet-wide earthquakes struck Eryndor. The already ancient Ironspine mountain ring amplified and transmitted aftershocks approximately tenfold globally. Extreme-western Avarran lowlands rose into new mountains; these are not the Ironspine. Many individuals perished, but no existing species was wiped out. An unnamed magic helped prevent extinction; its mechanism remains open.

records.title: The Created Southern Volcano
records.summary: Created by the dark mages at the start of the Era of Fire.
records.body: Created by the dark mages at the start of the Era of Fire. The end-of-Age earthquakes intensified it. Mages harnessed and restrained its potential eruption, limiting destruction but unknowingly increasing their own magical power. The intervention does not guarantee there was no eruption, damage or death.

records.title: Third Age Framework
records.summary: A proposed span of 8,873 years, using nine Avarran eras whose individual names, year ranges and events have not been finalized.
records.body: A proposed span of 8,873 years, using nine Avarran eras whose individual names, year ranges and events have not been finalized. This is a working framework, not universal era terminology.

records.title: Creation of the Orcs
records.summary: Sometime in the Third Age, surviving dark mages from the Southern Wastes created the Orcs/Urakai by an undecided method.
records.body: Sometime in the Third Age, surviving dark mages from the Southern Wastes created the Orcs/Urakai by an undecided method. Their aim was to besiege Khazari strongholds and eventually attack Eldar and human kingdoms. No Orc existed in either the First or Second Age. The objectives are confirmed, but whether particular assaults actually occurred is open.

records.title: Fourth Age Framework
records.summary: World Age immediately preceding the current Fifth Age.
records.body: World Age immediately preceding the current Fifth Age. Exact duration, chronology, disasters, kingdoms and transitions need development; do not manufacture a bridging history without a canon decision.

records.title: Fifth Age — Era of Crowns
records.summary: The campaign takes place in the Fifth Age, Year 3,847 of Avarra’s Era of Crowns.
records.body: The campaign takes place in the Fifth Age, Year 3,847 of Avarra’s Era of Crowns. The start of this era is not automatically the same as the start of the worldwide Fifth Age. Other current continental eras remain undecided.

records.title: Concord of Crowns
records.summary: An uneasy settlement among major powers has helped maintain peace for nearly two centuries before the campaign opening.
records.body: An uneasy settlement among major powers has helped maintain peace for nearly two centuries before the campaign opening. Exact treaty terms and signatories remain incompletely recorded; not all regions are peaceful.

records.summary: Historical Goblin and Ogre alliances with Orc forces, and the wars contributing to western prejudices, must be dated to the Third Age or later, because Orcs did not exist before then.
records.body: Historical Goblin and Ogre alliances with Orc forces, and the wars contributing to western prejudices, must be dated to the Third Age or later, because Orcs did not exist before then. Exact wars, leaders and dates are open.

records.title: Karak-Varn
records.summary: Independent Khazari Throne ruled by King Durgan IV Stonehand.
records.body:
Karak-Varn is one of the seven independent Khazari Mountain Thrones in the ancient Ironspine system. Current adopted sixfold resident/domain planning total: 22,800,000. Ruler: King Durgan IV Stonehand. Key industries and traditions: Iron and weapons, archives, mining, military engineering.

The reported total is a domain/metropolitan envelope, not necessarily only the core city. Exact urban/territorial population boundaries need mapping. Other Throne populations are part of the 132-million subtotal and must not be added again to the global Khazari figure.

records.title: Natural Magic — The Worlds Breath
records.summary: The planet itself creates pervasive Natural Magic, independent of lunar sources.
records.body: The planet itself creates pervasive Natural Magic, independent of lunar sources. Ordinary living things and materials participate in it to varying degrees. Deep understanding and training are still necessary for sophisticated use.

records.title: Lunar Magic and Moons
records.summary: The current system has around 221–255 moons (238 working midpoint).
records.body: The current system has around 221–255 moons (238 working midpoint). Moons themselves source lunar magic, but effects vary greatly: some nearly negligible, others powerful. Orbital location and alignment matter; individual domains remain largely unmapped.

records.title: First Age Lost Lunar Disciplines
records.summary: When older source-moons were destroyed, particular magical disciplines truly ceased to exist.
records.body: When older source-moons were destroyed, particular magical disciplines truly ceased to exist. They are not hidden spells that can simply be rediscovered. New fragment-moon magic is distinct.

records.title: Divine Magic and the Gods
records.summary: Gods of magic can govern, regulate or influence magical power without replacing the planet as the source of Natural Magic or the moons as the source of lunar power.
records.body: Gods of magic can govern, regulate or influence magical power without replacing the planet as the source of Natural Magic or the moons as the source of lunar power. The exact pantheon and links to moons remain unresolved.

records.title: Inherently Good, Grey and Evil Magic

records.body: Some magical forces themselves have good, morally ambiguous or evil natures; this differs from practitioners’ intentions or the moral standing of an entire people. Specific spell and deity classifications remain unfinished.

records.title: Magical Compatibility
records.summary: Distinct disciplines have real affinities and resistances.
records.body: Distinct disciplines have real affinities and resistances. Lunar alignment can strengthen or disturb interactions, but it does not create compatibility from nothing.

records.title: Ancient Harmonisation and Fusion
records.summary: A lost ancient technique used Natural Magic as a shared medium to fuse otherwise distinct disciplines into a unified working.
records.body: A lost ancient technique used Natural Magic as a shared medium to fuse otherwise distinct disciplines into a unified working. It predates the First Throne, is not exclusively Khazari, and cannot be assumed available to Gloin.

records.title: Current Campaign Pause
records.summary: Autumn Day 22, Year 3847, ~11:25 AM at Hadrik’s desk.
records.body:
The campaign is paused precisely at the Royal Historical Archive in Karak-Varn. Gloin Hammerfeld and Maela Deepforge stand at Hadrik Ironvein's desk, where he has asked what they uncovered. Gloin has not answered.

Gloin is 42, healthy, and has 10 silver crowns and 82 copper coins. Equipment: worn boots, clothes, personal axe, family keepsake of unknown significance, borrowed Foundations of First Throne Script, notebook and survey sketches. Borin holds the original survey.

Active practices: three First Throne runes (Hold, Within, Until Command); recognizes additional symbols without mastering them. Maela apprenticeship twice weekly if schedules allow; Keldrun civilian combat course three times weekly (next planned Day 23 morning); Bruni metallurgy lesson Day 23 at 11:30 AM. Elska's research is agreed but has not yet begun. No additional events occur before the player resumes.

records.title: Autumn Day 19 — Opening and Borin
records.summary: Gloin woke on an outdoor bench, considered jobs, and pursued Borin’s mine warning.
records.body:
The first verified scene opens at 7:20 AM, Autumn Day 19. Gloin, age 42, woke on a back-alley bench in Karak-Varn's Lower Eastern Quarter, not in the old superseded rented-room story.

A job board offered a mine expedition, merchant caravan and three-year Royal Army service. He considered enlisting but first followed Borin. Borin disclosed a closed mine, hidden chamber, three missing engineers and a preserved original survey. Gloin saw three survey sheets describing nine levels versus six on public maps. He hid and overheard Edrik Voss's alleged breach account. By morning he sought Hadrik's historical expertise; later he discussed runesmithing with Maela. No enlistment occurred.

records.title: Autumn Day 20 — Quarry and Research
records.summary: Borin taught practical engineering at Old Quarry Access, followed by study and training.
records.body:
Gloin met Borin at Old Quarry Access around 7 AM for underground structural instruction. They inspected ceiling fractures, damp, supports and wood timbers, then a repositioned survey marker bearing possible older First Throne geometry. This was NOT the sealed eastern mine. Breakfast followed.

In afternoon/evening Gloin consulted Hadrik and Maela, studied a dozen symbols (recognition, not mastery), practiced introductory axe control and pursued separate evidence. Some transaction times and original dialogue remain unrecovered.

records.title: Autumn Day 21 — Family Supper
records.summary: Family disclosures, eight-silver meal, metallurgy and discreet magical research commitments.
records.body:
Gloin held a large family supper with Durgan, Mara, Bruni, Tovin, Elska, Rurik, Harn and Vessa. He disclosed the eastern mine's survey differences, missing engineers, First Throne clues, political reports and his uncertainties.

The supper cost 8 silver; the latest confirmed post-supper purse is 10 silver 82 copper, though an earlier sum has an 11-copper unexplained discrepancy. Bruni agreed to a Day 23 metallurgy lesson and Elska to discreet historical Common Magic research. Family knowledge comes from this direct disclosure; outsiders do not automatically learn it.

records.title: Autumn Day 22 — Mine Inspection
records.summary: Non-invasive structural and resonance investigation; sealed door remained closed.
records.body:
Gloin woke at 4:30 AM and reached the eastern mine at approximately 5:52 AM. Maela, Rennik, Feldin and Orsa examined accessible passages and records, not the sealed chamber. The previously planned attendance included Edrik and Captain Vale but the difference remains unexplained.

Unusual vibration was strongest near a replacement drainage stone, recurrent about every 19–21 seconds; other western wall features and maintenance records needed follow-up. The team did not prove any entity, deliberate breach or global conspiracy. Maela and Gloin later compared stone samples. Finally they reached Hadrik's Royal Historical Archive desk at about 11:25 AM. The scene pauses before Gloin's reply.

records.title: Currency and Practical Economy
records.summary: 100 copper = 1 silver; 100 silver = 1 gold; 100 gold = 1 platinum.
records.body:
The standard four-coin accounting system uses copper, silver crowns, gold crowns and platinum crowns, at 100:1 steps. A common bed is 2 copper, basic room 5, comfortable room 8, quality inn 1 silver; breakfast 2–5 copper, hearty meal 4–6 copper, small ale 2 copper, honey brew 3 copper. Local conditions, supply, war, materials and bargaining affect prices.

Gloin's recorded purse must change only when actual transactions occur. Do not invent costs or silently alter the ledger.

records.title: Player Agency and Story Rules
records.summary: Gloin belongs to the player; NPCs act independently and mysteries have no preset answer.
records.body:
Only the player chooses what Gloin says, thinks, attempts, intends and decides. Narration may show consequences, fair risk, injuries, training, relationships, world reaction and independent NPC agency. No plot armor or guaranteed hero status. The world remains dark and gritty yet hopeful.

Always maintain chronology, exact inventory and money, source attribution, NPC knowledge boundaries and the current pause; do not advance the story during editorial work. Ancestry and possible descent from the First Throne remain genuinely unchosen. Dialogue prompts are options, not commands.

records.body: Ancient Khazari civilization with engineering and runic sophistication beyond many present institutions. Estimates of over 40 million at its height are uncertain. Its political dissolution, evacuation and final ruler’s fate remain unresolved.
